findings.claim: Requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes (e.g. [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[DataContract]) they are honoured. The collector ignores attributes on T entirely: it always uses contractless over public read-write members, or the surrogate. Attributes on T are never read, so the acceptance criterion is not met. Ledger L18 says to follow the requirement, so it does not excuse this.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator/execution test where T is decorated with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(5)] on a member, with a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class for it. Assert the serialized bytes use the declared key (array layout) rather than a string-key map.

findings.claim: Contractless mode skips public get-only properties and readonly fields. The requirement says contractless over public members, and ContractlessStandardResolver serializes them via a matching constructor. Constructor parameters are also never matched, so types with only parameterized constructors are rejected (MsgPack009). L19 says to follow the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a type with a public get-only property using ContractlessStandardResolver and using the generated formatter, then compare the bytes. The generated output omits the member.

findings.claim: The attribute lives in MessagePack.Annotations. A new public API plus the new MsgPack019-022 diagnostics require PublicAPI.Unshipped entries. The diff shows none for the new attribute, and the Unshipped analyzer release notes only list rules. Convention-wise this is likely missing.

receipt_plan.detail: Check whether PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt exists for MessagePack.Annotations and lacks GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute entries.

findings.claim: The collector reports MsgPack009 (NoDeserializingConstructor) and other existing diagnostics (MemberNeedsKey, DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys, KeysMustBeUnique) in the same way as for [MessagePackObject] types. Types from referenced assemblies being skipped by the TypeCollector is deliberate. Per L11, the consuming assembly generating no formatter for a metadata type is not a defect, and this attribute is an explicit opt-in.

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] metadata-only types get no automatic formatter; the explicit attribute is a separate opt-in path, so this is fine.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: The change implements contractless-by-default plus an optional SurrogateType. Attributes on T are ignored. Surrogate keys are matched by name and type. Only classes and structs with a parameterless constructor are supported.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Contractless-only with no surrogate. The collector reads [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[DataContract] on T when present, and falls back to contractless otherwise. The SurrogateType property, MsgPack022 and the surrogate code are removed. T's own attributes drive keys.
